items.title: REACTION | A respectable result under the circumstances | Trabzonspor 2-0 Hearts
items.text: Hello and welcome to Heart Standard and to Trabzon airport. It's about half 5 in the morning. I've just got here for a 7:20 flight. I've just done an all nighter. I was um planning to sleep. I got back about midnight, tried to sleep. Didn't happen. So, I decided just to do some work and then come to the airport nice and early for the first of my three flights back to Edinburgh. Although, I've just been informed that there's a a storm back home. So hopefully I'm not stranded in London like the last time I tried to come back via London. Just going to do a quick analysis of the game. I know that the story of the day is the injuries, but I think that's just a topic that probably deserves a much bigger discussion uh than I can give it just now. But suffice to say, it's really frustrating for the players involved, for Franken and these endless selection issues and for the fans who just want to see a competitive team out on the pitch and yeah, it's just not have to see players hit a bit of form and then drop out and not know who's going to be there from week to week and all that kind of thing. But something that I'm sure we'll dig into over the next few weeks. But looking back on last night's game, I think it's fair to say that everybody was fearing the worst or most people were fearing the worst. Although there was a suspicion that there could be some sort of reaction. And as I spoke to Blair about in the pre-match video, I think what Arts fans were looking for was at the very least keeping the score down because a defeat losing away to Travon Sport is not an embarrassment in of itself but to keep the score down and to put in a respectable performance and I think they got that and I think especially under the circumstances when you've got Natal at left back and then you play the majority of the game with Kingsley at left back sorry at right back and you're down to you're down to only two center halves again and you've only got one fit midfielder because Mendy was only fit enough for the bench and and the and the reason Kingsley's on the bench is because they're trying to manage his minutes and imagine that's what was going on with MC as well. So under the circumstances, I think it's a it's a it's a decent result and it's a performance that they can take encouragement from and hopefully go into Sunday's game and get a win because it becomes much more important that game now. I think with the recent run that they're on and the the games that are coming up after there's still quite a lot of difficult games after that. So you don't want to be going into playing Rangers one win in seven ideally and especially given the recent form of Motherwell their five straight defeats. So it's a it's a winnable game there to kind of get hearts back on track especially in the league where it sort of faltered a little bit recently. But looking at last night's game, don't know if you can analyze the lineup too much because Franklin was forced into a lot of what he was doing. But there was lots of eyebrows raised at Rogers M at left back. When I first saw it, the first thing that jumped out to me, jumped out at me was he's got pace. So that was probably one of the reasons he was there. I haven't necessarily thought of him as a as a great tackler or anything like that. So, it's not it it wasn't a role that I think he would I was necessarily thinking he would take to that well, but he is fairly decent in the air. So, there is that at least. But I think for the most part, he was really good. He won his first few battles against Salon. I think gave him a lot of confidence for the rest of the game. You saw that Salah started to drift into the pitch a we bit more in the midway through the first half and he was doing it a bit in the second half as well. Now Salah is probably going to do that anyway, but it was notable that he was sticking to the right at the start of the game and then after losing a couple of battles to Matt, he did start to move in at the center. Whether he would have just done that anyway or whether um it was because of the attention of Matt, I'm not entirely sure. But either way, it was a really good performance from Matau. Couple of shaky moments here and there, it's largely very, very good. and going the other way as well. It meant that when he over overlapped and when he got forward because he's an attacker, he was a good attacking outlet as well at times. And relatedly, I'd say that was that was maybe maybe the only criticism, maybe not the only criticism, but maybe the main criticism of hearts on Thursday night there was the lack of efficiency in the final third, which you've seen in a few games this season and especially in games like this. If you want to get anything from them, you're going to have to take your chances. And that goes for Malachi Fagen Walcott's header which comes off the base of the post. I mean, he's really unlucky with it. And that goes for um when Josh Mate got in behind towards the end and he sort of had a cross come shot that went between both JJ Williams um and the goal and went wide. Those kind of chances you've got to kind of be taken if you want to take anything from those kind of matches. Um elsewhere, your Delta was another really good performance. I mean, not quite a square peg in a round hole like it was with Rogers Mato. He's played the position before. He's played just about every position and he's such a good footballer that you can probably drop him in just about anywhere and he'll he'll do a good job. But I thought he was particularly good, especially alongside Magnus. you know that Magnus maybe isn't quite as good on the ball as some of the other midfielders like Azou and and Alton I know Alton is not a midfielder for the the sake of conversation here and even like someone like Mendy but I thought they were they were they were a decent partnership for each other I mean Magnus I think Magnus still has a bit of growing into this team if he's going to find a place in it um there's still too many times where he kind of gives the ball sloppily and the the main black mark against Thomas Magazine really was the penalty he gave away. It was a bit needless. There was other covering defenders there. It was not necessarily they had to make that challenge and he's just clumsily went through the back. I think that's how you say it. Um and hearts had largely kept transone sport quiet until then and I know they kind of grew into the half as it progressed but had a couple of saves but they were they were fairly comfortable. Sorry if this is a bit shaky. I just had to find some we corner in the uh in the airport here. But yeah, Bo Rouse was um largely comfortable and it took a penalty for for Trapsport to take the lead. They very well may have before Halime anyway given that they were starting to dominate a bit more. And then in the second half it was a bit more sitting in soaking up pressure and trying to hit on the break. And the second goal was just a bit of quality really. It's a really nice one too. The finish is it's just a beautiful finish from a really good striker they've paid a lot of money for and it's kind of game over from then and you did fear a wee bit that they could kind of push on a bit and get a few more goals but thankfully Hart stood firm and managed to keep the score down which could actually be important. It does depend on whether hearts can start picking up some wins in this tournament, but as we saw two years ago, goal difference can be a factor. So, the fact that they haven't lost heavily to one of the better sides that they're going to face away from home could could very well benefit them when it comes to qualifications. That said, the big caveat of they're going to have to go to Ton or Pathos and win in all likelihood if they're going to be in with a shout of qualifying. Anyway, back to the game. I'm trying to think if there was anything else in particular. Um, I thought the center backs largely did a good job. There was a few moments that Fegan Walker almost played some wood through at one point, but Mart managed to um managed to cover. I'm hoping that the more that they play together, the more of a partnership will blossom. Franken does seem to be a fan of the two of them. So, he sees something in them that he thinks can develop into a partnership. He's played both of them most games where they've been available certainly all games in the case of Malachi Fagan Walcott at center half I think Jeremy Mart to fill in at left back a few times um instead of at center back but he's largely paid I mean I looked it up earlier he's already doubled the number of minutes that he played in the entirety of last season. I know it was a bit of a difficult season for him to get into the team last season, but yeah, it's um it's quite something that he's already managed to double his minutes this season. Um, and to follow on from in the in the the issues in the final third, I thought Braga was improved, but again, there are times where hearts need him to be better at taking the ball in and keeping the ball. There's still too many times where he'll get it and then lose it quite quickly. But that said, there were other times where he did muscle his way past an opponent or he did turn and drive in a bit of space and it's been a bit of an up and down season for him, but I think that was a a bit of an improved performance and hopefully he can take confidence from that and kick on from there. I don't know if I've left anybody else. Wilson had a wee bit of a quiet game, a quieter game I guess. Um although a lot of the balls into him, especially in the first half, were sort of balls in behind for him to chase and things like that. So it maybe wasn't the the easiest shift for him, especially against a a team of that caliber. Should be said as well. I meant to say this earlier that Trabzons were weren't at their best. That's maybe partly down to them making quite a lot of changes. But yeah, overall uh positive performance, not a terrible result, although it is another defeat. It is 1 and six now. But hopefully there's enough nuggets of positivity in there that they can take encouragement from into Motherwell on Sunday and get a positive result from there. a venue that they didn't win it last season, but as I said, it's it didn't look like a very easy game when the fixtures came out at the start of the season and a few weeks into the season given the way the mother well started, but given the way they've been playing recently, it's a very winnable game coming up on Sunday. I will leave it there. I'm sorry this was a bit rambling. I'm not used to doing these solo ones. Used to have somebody to to bounce off. Check everything out. UK. Plenty going up there. Reaction from the game. There'll be more going out over the coming days and in the buildup to the game on the Sunday. Please check out back here for more videos and we will see you all

items.title: PREVIEW | Signing of Salah a Turkish SOAP OPERA | Trabzonspor v Hearts
items.text: Hearts are back in European action this week when they fly to Turkey to take on Trabzonspor in the Conference League. We are going to preview that match the Hearts standard and to do so I'm delighted to be joined by Trabzonspor supporter Yakup Marufoglu. How are you doing Yakup? I'm good Craig. Thanks for having me. Yeah, thanks for coming on. We're looking to get your insight into the club that you support and we're recording this right after the full-time whistle of Trabzonspor two Besiktas nil. The result takes Besiktas Sorry, takes Trabzonspor above Besiktas into fourth place. Level on points with third place Fenerbahce. What were your thoughts on the performance from Trabzonspor tonight? Um well, if I can recommend one game to watch from the Super League every year it should be the games the games between Trabzonspor and Besiktas. They are always a great game for the neutral supporter. Um but we have been playing quite well the last couple of games since we got the new manager. So I was a little bit anxious but the team didn't disappoint. We played a pretty decent match. At times Besiktas was better. They probably deserved a goal or two but we stayed consistent. Onana had a wonderful match and our defense was like rock steady. So you just have to make the chances that you get. So you have to be clinical in front of goal and we we were. We missed a couple of great chances too but with the crowd back at home and the players just performing really well it's just the confidence that they just pulled us through. We were talking about Onana just before we came on air there and you've mentioned him. He did have a very good game. What's what's his time been like in Turkey because what a lot of even Scottish football fans with them England just being on the doorstep, their only experience of Onana will have been that slightly disastrous spell at Manchester United. But what's he been like since he signed for Trabzonspor? Well, I've known him since he played at Ajax because I'm from I'm from the Netherlands. So, I I've always know I always known that that he has been a good keeper. Um the the the the environment at Manchester is just really toxic. So, it depends on that even doesn't even depend how good you are of a player. Uh you always tend to get get crumbled by all the pressure that you have. Um last year when we went for him, I wasn't that supportive to be honest. But he he from the first moment to I think his first game was against Fenerbahçe or something and he played he played really well. He has embraced the city. He He has embraced the fans. And every now and then like the last game that we had against KuPS, he had he he he conceded a goal straight from from a corner kick. He has his moments as he always tends to have. But whenever we play with him, the the saves that he has, the the way he's on the ball and he can distribute the ball is just unbelievable. Uh there are not that many keeper keepers in the world uh that that that are able to to distribute the ball as well. Um so, I'm really happy. He's He's really calm on the ball and it helps our defense is pretty good at also. So, it it helps to alleviate the pressure from the defense a little bit. So, he's he's he's known to play on in the big stage. So, uh the pressure doesn't seem to get to him. And because the fans and the city and pretty much everyone at Trabzon has been supportive of him, it it feels like he has he has let his shoulders down a little bit so he can be a little bit more calm on the ball and and get that presence that brought him with Inter like to the to to the Champions League finals, you know? And just before we go on to talk about the season a wee bit more generally, I wanted to ask you about the identity of the club because it seems to be quite an interest and they have quite an interesting place in Turkish football, Trabzonspor. So, can you explain to me what the club's identity is and kind of how how they fit into to Turkish football? So, Trabzonspor was founded by the merger of of three teams. And the city of Trabzon has always been known for its nationalism, so to say. So, they they everybody that's from from Trabzon proud itself of being from the city. Um so, when when Turkish football started, the Istanbul teams Besiktas, Galatasaray, and Fenerbahce dominated it for for decades. And when Trabzonspor was founded, they they rose through the ranks so quickly that when they first reached the the the the the premier division of the of the Turkish league, they they won like three or four Champions League they won three or four titles back-to-back. So, it has been known for for years now to be the one that destroyed the Istanbul hegemony. Um and we are known to have really passionate fans. And people, as I say, they they they they just live and breathe with the city. Whenever Trabzonspor does well, the city feels alive. Everybody's happy. You won't see a frown anywhere. But when they do awful, the whole city is down. So, we are known for our for our passion, always have been. And when we have players that are from the city, they tend to bring a certain passion with them. They they they they seem to go the extra yards for for everybody, for the fans, because they grew up with the with the team and with the city, and they know how much it how much it means to them. Um we had a couple couple couple seasons that that that that that broke the that broke the the city and the and the team, so to to And ever since money became a much bigger topic in football and the finances between the there's a big difference between Istanbul or Trabzon just city wise and demographic wise it's not a rich city it's pretty poor to be honest but people tend to spend their last last cents to go to a game. But it it became much more difficult for Trabzonspor to to to fight against the bigger establishment. But through perseverance uh dedication and everything we just pushed through and every now and then it it it just gives a different vibe. Whenever people are able to visit Trabzon they they tend to see it because you can't walk a meter without without seeing a Trabzonspor flag. So, so from what you're saying there, was Fatih Terim was he was he against some of the signings that were made in the summer because they were big names in the like because they were signing maybe from what his perception that they were just signing big names rather than trying to put a team together? Yeah, the there has been an internal struggle. It looked like a Turkish soap opera every now and then to be honest. We had like the head scout that we had which brought players like Ulai, Augusto, a lot of like talented young players. They got pretty much into like a battle for who is the manager or that's what they say to be honest. So, nobody will know the the whole truth. But, it was told that there was like internal struggle about who is the manager and who who decides what. And you need a coach that has been through this through this through this like pushing and pulling for years. So so so he he had to be confident, but it it it just didn't work out which I'm a little bit heartbroken by because I used to watch his games back in the day and I I really loved him as a player and as a and as a person he he seems to be from from everything that I heard a really good a really good person. items.text: Well, that was a disaster. Hello and welcome to Hearts Standard as we reflect on the chastening and embarrassing 7-1 defeat to Celtic on Sunday afternoon at Celtic Park. We'll hopefully won't take up too much time, but there's a lot to get through. I'm going to get I'm going to start with the closest thing to positive out the way first. First contact That's something that Hearts have been pretty good at recently from attacking set pieces is getting first contact, which is big. And then on the second say the second goal, Hearts did get first contact on the set piece, but the reaction after that was was relatively poor. items.title: CLAUDIO BRAGA | Striker staying positive during tough run of games | Hearts 1-1 Nordsjaelland
items.text: It is actually uh feel like first half we did a very good first half. Uh creates more chances than just the one nil. Uh we could go with two nil, but of course they are a very good opposition. They play very good football. Second half uh they had more ball and we knew they could create dangers when they had the ball. That's their game, so hope we hope that the goal didn't come uh but but yeah, they were they were a little bit on top of us in the last minutes and yeah, disappointing. Is it disappointing that you couldn't the manager couldn't make the subs just before it cuz there were there were a lot of players tired? Yeah. It's like of course uh I feel like we we run a lot in the second half. Uh this style of game uh obligates you to to run without ball also to make a lot of movements and with the ball just to press high also. So, it's kind of uh hard hard style of game to do it, so we need of course we're going to get tired if we do it properly. I think we did and then yeah, just disappointed to suffer the goal in that moment. Was one of the frustrations not scoring another goal when you were on top? Yeah, of course uh but to be honest like I feel one nil was deserved. Could be more, but I feel we were uh we were doing we were doing good. But yeah, definitely you need to be more efficient in a way, but I don't think we we missed that many, you know, but yeah, definitely wanted to score more. You had a chance just before half time. Yeah, just left-footed. Uh and you know, when I when I shot straight away I I thought like just need to chop inside and hit it with the right. But yeah, just these kind of moments that you need to think in half a second, so yeah. You have to regroup now, Claudio, for Sunday. Yeah, of course. Ready are you ready is the team for that game now? Ready, I think like of course this is disappointing, but it's a very good team we played against European competition uh and uh yeah, they played today also, so we we can't have the excuse of being tired or anything. Um we had the same the same minutes as them in the same day, so I I feel like we we are ready already, you know? Already are you mentally for another trip to Celtic Park after the last season in it? We're ready. I feel like at least for what I feel, nobody's thinking about that because we can't, you know? You get too emotional and it's not good uh, when you get too emotional. Of course, emotions come to football, but not good when you get too emotional. So, we just need to think about like, okay, it's a good opposition in the league right now. Uh, nothing to do with last year. Just we need to go there and try to get the points uh, this year. So, yeah. So, you're very different. You don't go there on Sunday probably means maybe only you and Harry who were involved Is that a good thing? So many guys aren't scarred by by what happened there? Yeah, in a way like I feel and I believe Harry feels the same uh, first weeks are still a little bit I hurt a lot, you know, like because it was a full year fighting for that, but after that you look back after two, three weeks and you just look back and you feel like, oh, we did something really good. So, if you just focus on the positives about that, you don't even remember that night. There's nothing to do now, so just focus on what we can control. Do you put it down as like you go there with a completely clean slate and have all those thoughts of flashback out of your mind completely? Yeah, of course. It's a different team uh, different coach, different players, uh, different style, uh, different year. So, everything is different to be honest. Just can't think about what happened uh, 1999 or last year. It doesn't really matter which year happened, so just focus on what happened this year and that's that's it. Do you know if that's a personal motivation or just to try and get a result? Nah, I Like the motivation is there already, you know, like he's playing uh, first against third, you know, like it's just like we we're going to play in a tough stadium. We know that, tough opposition, but that's it. The motivation is already there. We don't we don't need to think about what happened before to get motivated. As you say, very different type of Hearts team that's going there. How different and in what ways is the team different even though it's only a few months since then? I think a different team are going to Celtic. A different style, different players, different coach, different tactics. I think very almost everything is different, you know, the starting players compared to last year, maybe like you said, like three, four guys who are who are in the team. So, just everything is different, so it's completely different Hearts. At the same time, we want to to achieve what we achieved there last year. When you look at Celtic, do you feel they're vulnerable and do you feel Hearts can go there and get a result? I wouldn't say vulnerable. Of course, like they have their vulnerabilities like we have and I'm sure they are analyzing that like we are analyzing their vulnera- vulnerabilities. Oh, word. And and yeah, just of course, they have like we have, but every team have even Barcelona and everything. So, but they are not they are not like a weak team or something like that. Maybe they go sometimes to a bad moment or we had these last two games when you like Falkirk and the game before, like maybe people were going like oh, it's a bad moment, but it's happened, you know, football. So, they're still a good team and they're still a hard sta- stadium to go. Does going there and getting a victory give you the confidence to think we're going to be back in this again this year? I think we have that confidence already, to be honest. Of course, that'll be a good statement, but this 5-0 against St. Mirren, the full position that we're up there is also a statement. Of course, going there, win that game against the team that is now first place is a good statement, for sure, but I think when we look when I talk with the guys in the locker room and the idea that we pass to each other is that we want to repeat what we did last year, but a little bit better. It's a challenging week next week, obviously with Celtic and then the trip to Turkey for the Hearts team, Trabzonspor. It's some week. Yeah, but to be honest, it's like if you look at the month of October, it's a very tough month, but like when you're a kid, you just dream with that. Just like playing every time big games, big games, and never drop the level. I think that's just a dream, to be honest. Just focus on the positive of that instead of like, "Oh, it's going to be tough opponents." And it will be, but it's also like very good. You You dream with this, you know? It means that you are between the best, so that's good.
